1.from: Grade 3 builds the facts; Grade 4 extends to factor pairs and multi-digit products.
1.to: Grade 7 proportional reasoning and Grade 8 linear equations assume these are instant.

2.from: Grade 3 places whole numbers; Grade 4 reads scaled line plots; Grade 5 partitions intervals.
2.to: Grade 7 uses the line for signed arithmetic; Grade 8 for irrational approximation.

items.q: 0 to 20 in 5 equal jumps — one jump is worth?
0 to 100 in 4 equal jumps — one jump?
0 to 1 in 10 equal jumps — one jump?
−10 to 10 in 4 equal jumps — one jump?

3.from: Grade 5 establishes powers of 10 and decimal place value.
3.to: Grade 7 percent change and Grade 8 scientific notation run on the same shift.

4.from: Grade 4 equivalent fractions; Grade 5 pattern tables.
4.to: Grade 7 constant of proportionality and Grade 8 slope are this move, named differently.

5.from: Grade 5 introduces Quadrant I and ordered pairs.
5.to: Grade 7 scale drawings and Grade 8 functions live entirely on this plane.

items.q: From the origin, 5 right and 2 down is…
If each gridline is 5, where is 35?

6.from: Grade 4 compares whole numbers; Grade 5 compares decimals to thousandths.
6.to: Grade 7 orders rational numbers including negatives in context.

7.from: Grade 4 introduces fractions with denominator 100; Grade 5 links them to decimals.
7.to: Grade 7 percent increase, discount, and interest all start here.

items.q: 3/4 as a decimal and a percent
0.05 as a percent and a fraction
1/5 as a decimal and a percent
40% as a fraction in simplest form

8.from: Grade 5 evaluates numerical expressions with grouping symbols.
8.to: Grade 7 multi-step equations and Grade 8 function rules depend on it completely.

9.from: Grade 4 fact families; Grade 5 properties of operations.
9.to: Grade 7 two-step equations and Grade 8 systems rest on the same undo-and-check.

10.to: Grade 7 statistics and Grade 8 data work still end in one careful sum.

11.from: Grade 3 tiles rectangles; Grade 4 applies the area formula; Grade 5 finds volume.
11.to: Grade 7 circles and composite figures; Grade 8 volume of cones and spheres.

items.q: Area of a triangle, base 7, height 4
Is the slanted side ever the height?

12.from: Grade 5 multiplies fractions and divides unit fractions by whole numbers.
12.to: Grade 7 operations with rational numbers assume all of it.
